Introduction:

Woodbridge Municipal Court is a city courthouse in Middlesex County, New Jersey. It is situated in the Woodbridge Township Municipal Building. It has jurisdiction over criminal, civil, traffic, vehicle and speeding matters. It is one of the busiest courts in New Jersey and has received a lot of traffic violation summons and criminal cases. This court provides in-person and virtual court sessions for cases. The court is an independent government branch that serves every visitor with fair and equal manners and provides justice according to the law.

How to find records information?

Woodbridge Municipal Court record information for cases are available in the town clerk’s and county clerk’s offices and found online on different websites. All the case information and trails are recorded and maintained by the county and clerk’s office. They can be searched online by using the following ways:

  • Searching by case number
  • Searching by name and city/state
  • Searching by address
  • Searching by phone
  • Searching by email

Sometimes, case information records are unavailable online because it is confidential according to the law, like criminal cases etc. These types of information are only available at the county court or county clerk’s office. They can be obtained by filing and sending a public record request form. Fill in all your personal information on the form. You had to describe in detail why you need these records. Send the fees for the copies of the record. Please read all the details before sending me the form. After receiving the form, the court will respond with whether to provide this information. For more information about the public records, call or mail the court.

How to make payments?

Woodbridge Municipal Court pays tickets and fines payment can be made in the following ways:

In-Person

A person can pay for tickets and fines by visiting the court during regular court hours and paying in cash, checks, or with a card at the violation bureau counter. Take your ticket when you are coming for payment. 2.99% processing and other charges will be applied if you make payment with a credit card. 

Online

Woodbridge Municipal Court pay ticket online can be made using the New Jersey Online Payment Portal

Enter the case or ticket number, license plate number, valid credit card information and court code. The service fees will be applied in this case.

Mail

A Person can send a certified check or money order to the court’s Violation Bureau mailing address, 1 Main St, Woodbridge Township, NJ 07095, United States. Cash or personal checks are not acceptable in the mail; only certified checks or money orders are accepted. Remember to write your citation when you send the payment, and mail the amount in a self-addressed, stamped envelope if you want a receipt.

Drop Box

You can also put payment in a self-addressed, stamped envelope and drop it in the drop box located in the municipal building.

What is the process of appealing?

Woodbridge Municipal Court appealing facility against the case decision is available. You had to file an appeal within 20 days of your case result at the Superior Court of Middlesex County. Appealing fees must be paid at the required time. All the information for this process is available in the booklet. The process is a bit difficult, so you must contact an attorney. Contact the Middlesex County Superior Court, Criminal Records, and Case Management Office for further information.

Phone: 732-519-3853

When appearing in court is necessary?

Woodbridge Municipal Court appearance is necessary when you are involved in a criminal, accident, or hit-and-run case or enters a plea of not guilty. You can dispose of a traffic ticket by appearing in court if the court orders that it is necessary to appear or can pay a fine online or by mail, or by paying at the counter, and your traffic ticket case will be solved.

How can I send a plea by mail?

Woodbridge Municipal Court plea can only be written if you received a traffic infraction, vehicle, speeding, or parking ticket. Write a plea and send it before the citation date written on your ticket. Download the plea form, choose the plea you want, write your name and email address, date, ticket/ complaint number, date and sign your signature. Two types of plea can be written and mailed to the court that are:

Plea of Guilty

Choose a guilty plea if you admit you violated the law or committed a crime. The court will review your application and respond with the fine amount or, in severe cases, with a court date. You had to describe in detail an explanation of guilt.

Plea of Not Guilty

If you do not accept your offense and deny all the violations against you, then choose the plea of not guilty. You had to write the explanation in detail to prove you were innocent and send the proof with the plea form. The court will review your application and send you a schedule for your court appearance, and you have to appear on time. Firstly a trial date is given to you, and you must appear with all the proof in your defense. Hire an attorney in this case.

How can I apply for the marriage ceremony?

Woodbridge Municipal Court marriage ceremonies are performed by the judges of this court. You had to make an appointment for the marriage ceremony by calling or coming to the clerk’s office counter. You must have the marriage license when you come for the appointment. After the schedule was decided, the couple had to come to the clerk’s office at 10:30 with two witnesses. Only 8 people are allowed in the ceremony if you take more than you had to wait for a long time.

FAQ:

What is the contact number of the clerk?

Woodbridge Municipal Court clerk’s contact number is 732-602-6007. You can call or visit the clerk’s office during working hours if you need any information.

Which things do the violation schedules hold?

Woodbridge Municipal Court violation schedules include: 

  • Statute or number of violations
  • Alleged offense description
  • The total ticket cost
What is the cost of the Exemplified Certificate of Disposition?

$10 is the cost of the Exemplified Certificate of Disposition.

How can I file a complaint?

Woodbridge Municipal Court complaint against someone can be filed by completing all the information on the Citizen’s Complaint form and sending it online or by mail to the court.

What can I do if I receive a complaint form from any person?

If you received a complaint form, you had to appear in court on the schedule; you can also bring an attorney and some proof proving you are innocent.

How can I search for cases?

Woodbridge Municipal Court case search can be done online by using first and last names with the date of birth and entering the state or city.
